transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess it’s the elevator thing. I mean, I know in my head they’re not really dangerous—people ride them all day, even at work sometimes when we’re hauling stuff around buildings—but when I have to actually get in one, I just get this fear like I’m going to be trapped in there. And I can’t seem to talk myself into feeling normal about it, even though I know it doesn’t make much sense.
Do you experience similar feelings of fear or anxiety in other situations, like being in crowded places, leaving your home, or being in open spaces, or is this mostly just about elevators?

It’s mostly the elevators, yeah. Like, I can be around job sites with people everywhere, or outside in big open lots, and that doesn’t really get me the same way. It’s just when I’m standing there waiting for an elevator, I start thinking, what if I get stuck in there? 

Which is funny, I guess, because I’ve been in way tighter spots at work—storage rooms, trailers full of tools, all that—but an elevator just hits different. I know they’re not actually dangerous, but once I have to step in, I can’t make myself feel normal about it.
Do you find yourself avoiding elevators altogether, or going out of your way to not use them, even if it’s inconvenient?

Yeah, I do. Most days I just take the stairs, like at our apartment or on job sites. Sometimes that’s fine, I mean, it’s probably good exercise anyway, though after hauling stuff all day my knees don’t exactly love it.

But yeah, if the elevator or one of those lifts is the only way to get up, I’ll usually try to get out of it somehow—ask if I can do a different part of the job or have somebody else take that task. If I absolutely have to ride it, I can do it better if someone I trust is right there with me. Otherwise I just… I really don’t want to get in.

When you're in or think about getting into an elevator, do you ever feel a sudden rush of intense fear or panic, like your heart races, you can't breathe, or you feel like you need to escape right away?

Yeah… I mean, not like I’m screaming or anything, but as soon as those doors start sliding shut, my chest gets tight and my hands get all sweaty. I’ll be standing there thinking, “Okay, it’s just a few floors,” but then my brain goes straight to, “I need to get out.”

It’s weird because at work I can deal with noisy equipment and all kinds of stuff, and that doesn’t bother me the same way. But in the elevator, once the doors close, it just feels like I need out right then.
